q: If a body is dropped from a height above the surface of the earth, it will fall onto the ground. This is due to the force of _____.
e: Bodies fall to the ground due to the gravitational force of the earth.

q: The weight of a body is the force of gravity acting on it which gives its acceleration when it is _____.
e: Weight is the gravitational force that causes acceleration when a body is falling.

q: The acceleration due to the force of gravity is called acceleration due to gravity and it is represented by the symbol _____.
e: Acceleration due to gravity is represented by the symbol g.

q: In MKS system, the value of g is approximately _____ m s⁻².
e: The acceleration due to gravity g ≈ 9.8 m s⁻² (or 9.8 N kg⁻¹).

q: In MKS system, the value of g can also be expressed as 9.8 _____ kg⁻¹.
e: The acceleration due to gravity can be expressed as 9.8 N kg⁻¹.

q: In FPS system, g = _____ ft s⁻².
e: In the FPS system, acceleration due to gravity g = 32 ft s⁻².

q: The attracting force of the earth acting on a body is defined as the _____ of the body.
e: Weight is defined as the gravitational force exerted by the earth on a body.

q: If the mass of the body is m and a=g, the weight of the body is found to be w=_____.
e: Weight is calculated using the formula w = mg, derived from Newton's second law.

q: The relation w=mg is true not only for freely falling bodies but also for bodies on the _____.
e: The weight formula w=mg applies to all bodies, whether falling or at rest on the ground.

q: Weight is a _____ and is directed toward the center of the Earth.
e: Weight is a vector quantity with direction toward the center of the Earth.

q: Since weight is force, units of weight are newton, dyne and _____, while the units of mass are kilogram, gram and slug.
e: Units of weight (force) are newton, dyne, and pound; units of mass are kg, g, and slug.

q: _____ is the quantity of matter in a body.
e: Mass is defined as the quantity of matter contained in a body.

q: Mass is also a measure of _____.
e: Mass measures the inertia of a body - its resistance to changes in motion.

q: The mass of a body measures its _____.
e: The mass of a body is a measure of its inertia.

q: The mass of a body defined from the point of view of measuring inertia is called _____ mass.
e: Mass defined as a measure of inertia is called inertial mass.

q: The mass defined by $m = \frac{W}{g}$ is called _____ mass.
e: Mass defined by the ratio of weight to gravitational acceleration is called gravitational mass.

q: Mass is a _____ and always a constant.
e: Mass is a scalar quantity and remains constant regardless of location.

q: Wherever a body may be, there is _____ change in the value of the mass of the body.
e: Mass is constant and does not change with location.

q: The weight of the body _____ change when its location is changed, but mass does not.
e: Weight can change with location (due to varying g), but mass remains constant.

q: Mass and weight are two _____ quantities.
e: Mass and weight are fundamentally different physical quantities and should not be confused.

q: According to Newton's law of gravitation, the gravitational force acting on a body at Earth's surface is $F = G \frac{mM}{R^2}$ where M is the mass of the _____ and R is the radius of the Earth.
e: In the formula, M represents the mass of the Earth and R is Earth's radius.

q: The value of g near the earth's surface is calculated as g = G × M/R² = _____ m s⁻².
e: Using G=6.67×10¹¹, M=5.97×10²⁴ kg, R=6.37×10⁶ m, we get g=9.8 m s⁻².

q: Note that the value of g is independent of the _____ of the body.
e: The acceleration due to gravity g is independent of the properties (mass, composition) of the falling body.
